LEGAL

Privacy & Cookies

How we handle website, early-access and Atomic service information.

Privacy notice · 3 November 2026

On this page1. Who and what this covers2. Website and early-access information3. Information used in the Atomic service4. Recipients, AI processing and transfers5. Retention, deletion and your rights6. Cookies and browser storage

1. Who and what this covers

Abstract Machines SAS, at the address in our company details, is the controller for the website, early-access requests and the account, service-administration, security and billing activities described here. Contact privacy@absmach.eu.

This notice also covers use of the Atomic application-building service when access is provided. The service information below applies to the features you use; a feature described here is not a promise that it is available in every account or plan.

When we process personal data in customer content or customer applications on a customer’s behalf, the customer, or the controller it represents, determines the purposes and our role is governed by the agreed DPA and processing schedule. This notice does not replace that agreement or the customer’s own notices to its app users.

2. Website and early-access information

The application form collects your name, email, app idea, project type/stage and role; company/project name is optional. Required fields let us assess and answer your request. Do not include third-party personal data or secrets in a waitlist application. We also record submission time, consent version and campaign-source parameters. Hosting and abuse protection process IP addresses, browser signals and request metadata.

  • Application review and related trial emails: your consent; this does not subscribe you to unrelated marketing.
  • Limited product research, campaign-source analysis, support and security: our legitimate interests in understanding demand and operating the service.
  • Optional audience/advertising measurement: your separate cookie consent.
  • Legal records and disputes: applicable legal obligations or legitimate interests in legal claims.

You can withdraw consent without affecting prior lawful processing. We do not sell early-access application information or make solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects in reviewing those applications.

3. Information used in the Atomic service

  • Accounts and collaboration: identity and contact details, profile information, authentication and session records, workspace membership, invitations and permissions. If you choose an available external sign-in option, it can supply an identifier, email and profile information such as a display name or photograph.
  • Creating applications: prompts and conversations, generated responses and source code, saved versions, comments, uploaded images and design references, and other project content you provide. These support generation, editing, previews, collaboration and project history.
  • Voice dictation, when used: recorded audio is sent for transcription, and the returned text can be reviewed before it is submitted as a prompt.
  • Running the service: build, preview and publication activity, diagnostic and security logs, support correspondence and usage records, such as account/app identifiers, request timing, resource consumption and outcomes. Logs can contain project or user context.
  • Billing, when applicable: plan, subscription, payment-reference, transaction and accounting records used to administer accepted paid offers.
  • Customer applications: app-user identities, permissions and business records that the customer chooses to collect or store. Personal data handled on the customer’s behalf is subject to its instructions and the agreed DPA.

For processing where we act as controller, we rely on performance of our contract with you, or steps you request before it, for necessary account and service delivery. Where an organization is the contracting customer, we rely on our legitimate interests in administering that relationship and enabling its authorized users. Security, abuse prevention, troubleshooting and service administration rely on our legitimate interests in operating a reliable service; required accounting and legal records rely on applicable legal obligations. Optional tracking and any other activity requiring consent use a separate consent choice. Choosing a feature does not authorize unrelated marketing or another independent use of its content.

Account and authentication information needed to provide access is required; without it we cannot provide that access. Project content and optional features are your choice, but the requested feature may not work without the relevant input. Only supply personal data you are authorized to use. Sensitive personal data requires the express agreement and safeguards described in the DPA.

4. Recipients, AI processing and transfers

Authorized staff and providers receive information needed for their roles: hosting, storage, identity and access, email delivery, AI generation/transcription, support, and payment processing when enabled. For the website and waitlist, Cloudflare provides hosting and Turnstile bot protection; mailing-list and email providers handle applications and trial messages; Google provides optional measurement. Advisers or authorities may receive data when necessary for legal matters.

When you request an AI feature, relevant content is sent to the AI service configured for that feature. Depending on the request, this can include prompts, conversation context, source files, uploaded references or an audio recording for transcription. The customer DPA does not authorize independent use of customer personal data, including general model training. This is not a representation that every provider has identical retention or data-use settings; the applicable provider arrangements must be established before customer personal data is processed.

Providers may process data outside the EEA, including in the United States. Transfers require an applicable adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards such as EU standard contractual clauses and necessary supplementary measures. Contact our privacy email for the applicable safeguards and a copy.

For processing on a customer’s behalf, provider identities, functions, processing locations and transfer safeguards are supplied privately with the DPA schedule before authorization. Provider changes follow that agreement’s notice and objection procedure. Confidentiality does not remove statutory information or audit rights.

5. Retention, deletion and your rights

Retention follows the purpose of the information:

  • Early-access applications are kept while needed for the requested programme, subject to withdrawal or deletion requests. Limited consent and suppression records support those choices.
  • Account and workspace records support the account relationship and authorized access. Project conversations, uploaded references, source and versions support the requested project, collaboration and recovery features under the applicable service arrangements. These periods depend on whether the account or project remains active, deletion or closure requests, unresolved support or security incidents, applicable legal retention periods and ongoing claims.
  • Dictation recordings are processed for transcription. Retention of recordings and provider copies follows the applicable transcription-service arrangements, including any necessary security or abuse handling. Transcripts submitted as prompts follow project retention. Contact our privacy address for the arrangements that apply.
  • Diagnostic and security records are kept for the troubleshooting or incident-handling purpose that justifies them. Usage and billing records may remain where needed for accounting, legal obligations or disputes.
  • Customer personal data, including copies and backups, follows the documented instructions and return, deletion and backup arrangements in the agreed DPA schedule. Any legally required retention remains restricted to that purpose.

Deleting an app and closing an account are different actions; app deletion does not by itself delete every account, accounting or backup record. Downloading source code does not export app users or business data. Contact us about the relevant retrieval or deletion request and applicable retention criteria.

For information we control, you may request access, correction, erasure, restriction and portability where applicable; object to legitimate-interest processing and direct marketing; withdraw consent without affecting prior lawful processing; and give applicable instructions for data after death. Email privacy@absmach.eu or use the unsubscribe link for trial emails. We respond within the GDPR deadlines, normally one month; a justified extension of up to two further months will be explained within that first month. You may complain directly to the CNIL or another competent authority.

For personal data controlled by a customer, contact that customer first. We assist it under the DPA; if you contact us, we will help route your request to the appropriate controller.

6. Cookies and browser storage

On the marketing website, Cookie Preferences in the footer lets you accept, reject or change optional measurement. Analytics measures visits and completed requests; marketing measures campaigns. Both are off by default. Google Tag Manager loads only after an optional category is accepted. Each tag must respect its category.

  • Consent choice: local storage, up to six months, then requested again.
  • Theme choice: local storage until changed or cleared.
  • Documentation menu position: session storage, consumed on navigation or ending with the browser session.
  • Turnstile: browser signals for signup abuse protection, loaded at the final form step.

Website demo state and unsent waitlist form text stay in page memory and reset on reload. This does not describe saved conversations or project content in the Atomic service. The signed-in service uses authentication/session cookies for access and security; those necessary purposes are separate from optional measurement. Any optional tracking in the service requires its own applicable information and choice.

See the Google and Cloudflare privacy information.
